title: Power BI Capacity Memory Eviction
dataSources: Power BI activity events (`o365:management:activity` with `Workload=PowerBI`), Power BI REST Admin API (`/admin/groups`, `/datasets/refreshes`, `/capacities/refreshables`), on-prem data gateway `Mashup`/`GatewayInfo` logs, Premium capacity metrics.
app: Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Cloud Services / Microsoft 365 (`Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices`) for the Power BI activity log; Power BI REST Admin API and on-prem data gateway logs via HEC scripted inputs.
spl:
index=bi sourcetype=powerbi:capacity:metrics metric=memory_evictions
| bin _time span=1h
| stats sum(value) as evictions by capacityName, _time
| where evictions>0
| sort - _time
description: Counts dataset memory evictions on Premium capacities, a sign that active datasets exceed available memory and are being paged out, hurting first-query performance.
value: Frequent evictions cause the dreaded slow first load as datasets reload into memory; tracking evictions guides capacity sizing and dataset placement.
implementation: Ingest capacity memory metrics; schedule hourly; alert when evictions climb. Move large datasets to a dedicated capacity or reduce model size.
visualization: Timechart of evictions per capacity, table of worst offenders.

references.title: Power BI — Track user activities (audit log)

grandmaExplanation: We notice when Power BI runs low on memory and has to drop reports out of it, which is why some reports feel slow the first time you open them.
